original_value: AbstractAs the number of models for 3D indoor scenes are increasing rapidly, methods for generating the lighting layout have also become increasingly important. This paper presents a novel method that creates optimal placements and intensities of a set of lights in indoor scenes. Our method is characterized by designing the objective functions for the optimization based on the lighting guidelines used in the interior design field. Specifically, to apply major elements of the lighting guideline, we identify three criteria, namely the structure, function, and aesthetics, that are suitable for the virtual space and quantify them through a set of objective terms: pairwise relation, hierarchy, circulation, illuminance, and collision. Given an indoor scene with properly arranged furniture as input, our method combines the procedural and optimization‐based approaches to generate lighting layouts appropriate to the geometric and functional characteristics of the input scene. The effectiveness of our method is demonstrated with an ablation study of cost terms for the optimization and a user study for perceptual evaluation.

result.paraphrase: AbstractAs the number of models for 3D indoor scenes grows rapidly, generating lighting layouts has become increasingly important. This paper introduces a new method for determining the optimal placement and intensity of a set of lights in indoor scenes. The method is distinguished by objective functions for optimization that are designed around lighting guidelines from interior design. In particular, to incorporate the main elements of these guidelines, we identify three criteria—structure, function, and aesthetics—appropriate for virtual spaces and express them with objective terms: pairwise relation, hierarchy, circulation, illuminance, and collision. Using an indoor scene with properly arranged furniture as input, the method combines procedural and optimization-based approaches to produce lighting layouts suited to the scene’s geometric and functional characteristics. Its effectiveness is demonstrated through an ablation study of optimization cost terms and a user study for perceptual evaluation.
